07 / CODE LAB

ServiceNow Code Lab

Practical examples of ServiceNow scripting, client-server communication, automation, and integration patterns.

Portfolio demonstration examples

Server-side / Read operation

Query Active Priority 1 Incidents

Demonstrate server-side record querying using GlideRecord.

Technical explanation

Build the query

Initialize GlideRecord for incident. Each addQuery() adds a condition; together they select active priority 1 records.

Execute and read

query() runs the request. next() advances the cursor, and getValue() reads a field value from the current record.

Key considerations

GlideRecord runs on the server. Use selective filters and suitable indexes on large tables; this example limits output to 20 records, not a complete report. Avoid unnecessary logging, and use ACL-aware access when caller permissions must be enforced.

Server-side / Before insert Business Rule

Automatically Route VPN Incidents

Route an unassigned VPN incident through a reusable, configuration-driven lookup.

Technical explanation

Timing and record context

current is the record being saved. A before-insert rule sets values before persistence. previous represents earlier values on supported update contexts; this insert-only example does not use it, and it is unavailable in async rules.

Configuration owns the destination

The Script Include tab defines PortfolioAssignmentUtil. A synthetic network/vpn lookup row references the intended Network Support group; the rule contains no fixed group identifier.

Key considerations

Use the same application scope as the utility. Avoid current.update() and recursive saves. Preserve deliberate assignments, define a triage path for missing configuration, and choose one routing owner so Assignment Rules and Business Rules do not compete. Avoid unnecessary hard-coded sys_ids.

Browser / onChange Client Script on impact

Dynamic Form Behavior

Display an informational field message when impact changes to High.

Technical explanation

Respond in the browser

Configure an onChange Client Script for impact. getValue() reads the stored choice value; this example assumes High is '1'. showFieldMsg() places guidance beside that field.

Clear the right message

hideFieldMsg() clears field messages before reapplying the hint. clearMessages() is appropriate for form-level messages added with addInfoMessage() or addErrorMessage(); it does not replace field-message cleanup.

Key considerations

Client Scripts run in the user's browser and are not security controls. Coordinate field-message ownership so one script does not clear another script's advice. Prefer UI Policies for declarative field behavior, and validate important rules on the server too.

Browser ↔ Server / Synthetic guidance lookup

Retrieve Server Data from a Client Script

Fetch a synthetic support hint asynchronously and apply it to the form.

  1. Client Script
  2. GlideAjax
  3. Script Include
  4. Server Response
  5. Form Update

Technical explanation

An asynchronous contract

addParam() supplies the method through sysparm_name and sends the category. getXMLAnswer() invokes a callback with the server's answer, keeping the form responsive.

Client-callable server logic

The Script Include extends AbstractAjaxProcessor and must be configured as client callable. Use its correct API name across scopes; the example assumes both scripts are in the same scope.

Key considerations

Restrict callable access to appropriate authenticated users and roles. Validate every client parameter and return only authorized data. This deliberately returns allowlisted synthetic guidance, not private user data. Empty answers leave the form unchanged; define user-safe error feedback for real remote failures.

Server-side / Not client callable

Reusable Assignment Utility

Resolve one active support group from a governed routing lookup.

Technical explanation

Separate lookup from routing

The utility returns a group reference; its caller decides whether to assign the incident. Several Business Rules can reuse the lookup without copying query logic.

Maintain configuration once

u_portfolio_route is an illustrative custom table with active, category, subcategory, and assignment-group reference fields. Two matches signal ambiguity; absent, duplicate, or inactive destinations return an empty result.

Key considerations

Create the synthetic schema before use and restrict configuration edits. Enforce unique routing keys, validate caller inputs, and define fallback behavior. This server-only utility assumes a trusted caller; data permissions and cross-scope access need explicit review. Reuse improves maintainability without exposing the utility to browsers.

POST /api/now/table/incident

Create Incident through REST

Illustrate a Table API create request with synthetic incident data.

Technical explanation

Request contract

POST creates a record; GET reads and PATCH updates. Send Content-Type: application/json and Accept: application/json. Authenticate over HTTPS with an approved mechanism such as OAuth and a least-privilege integration identity.

Response handling

A successful create returns 201. The fictional result above is an abbreviated Table API response with identifiers omitted. Inspect errors and status: distinguish invalid input from authentication, permission, or server failures before retrying.

Key considerations

The path is relative and contains no instance address or credentials. Confirm category choices, required fields, ACLs, and Business Rules in the target instance. A successful HTTP response still needs field-level verification. Avoid blind retries of POST requests that could create duplicate incidents.

GOOD SERVICENOW DEVELOPMENT PRACTICES

Guidelines to adapt to the application, security model, and implementation requirements.

  • Avoid hard-coded sys_ids
  • Keep queries efficient
  • Reuse server-side logic
  • Use client-side scripting only when necessary
  • Validate inputs
  • Apply least-privilege access
  • Use meaningful naming conventions
  • Handle errors gracefully
  • Keep configuration separate from logic where practical
